institution.name: Northgate Utilities
institution.industry: Regulated electric utility — transmission and distribution

capability.name: Switching order verification
capability.description: The supervisor's demonstrated ability to independently verify a switching order against the network model and identify a conflicting condition before authorising work. The failure mode this capability guards against is a switching error, which is a leading cause of recordable injury in transmission and distribution operations.

business_metric.name: Total Recordable Incident Rate (TRIR)
business_metric.source_system: Northgate EHS incident management system, reconciled to OSHA 300A annual summary
business_metric.definition_notes: Standard OSHA formula: (recordable incidents x 200,000) / total hours worked. Calculation method confirmed with the metric owner and reconcilable to the filed 300A. Direction is DECREASE — a lower figure is better, which inverts the delta logic relative to a retention metric.

value_outcome.impact_basis: METHOD. Recordable incidents = TRIR x hours / 200,000. Over 4.1M hours worked in the measurement period, each 1.00 of TRIR equates to 20.5 incidents. Valued at Northgate's own fully-loaded cost per recordable incident of $423,000 — supplied and attested by Northgate FP&A, comprising direct medical, indemnity, crew downtime, investigation and regulatory response. Excludes insurance premium effect and reputational cost. CLAIMED figure derives from the committed target of 1.10 (6.56 incidents avoided). REALIZED figure derives from the measured actual of 1.08 (6.97 avoided). Attested, not independently audited.

evidence.summary: TRIR of 1.42 for the twelve months ended 31 January 2026 across the transmission and distribution field population.
evidence.provenance: Attested by R. Castellanos, Director EHS, Northgate Utilities. Drawn from the EHS incident management system and reconciled to the filed OSHA 300A.
evidence.source_reference: Northgate EHS export EHS-2026-0131; OSHA 300A FY2025

evidence.summary: TRIR of 1.08 for the twelve months ended 31 July 2026, same population and methodology.
evidence.provenance: Attested by R. Castellanos, Director EHS, Northgate Utilities. Same system and reconciliation basis as the baseline.

evidence.summary: Fully-loaded cost per recordable incident of $423,000, and 4.1M hours worked in the measurement period.
evidence.provenance: Attested by S. Bhatt, Director FP&A, Northgate Utilities. Derived from Northgate's own incident cost model.
evidence.source_reference: Northgate FP&A incident cost model, rev 2026.2

evidence.summary: Assessed switching order verification capability across 214 field operations supervisors moved from 2.1 to 3.9 on a 0-5 scale.
evidence.provenance: Coach-of-record assessment by M. Lindqvist, Manager Technical Training, Northgate Utilities. Scored against the published rubric; AI-assisted drafting of narrative feedback only.

evidence.summary: Twelve documented instances of supervisors halting a switching sequence after identifying a conflicting network condition.
evidence.provenance: Operations control room log review. Corroborating rather than primary; no attestation obtained.
evidence.source_reference: Northgate control room log sample, Mar-Jun 2026

assessment.population_note: Cohort assessment across 214 supervisors. The schema has no cohort object, so this attaches to the assessor of record with the population recorded here. Modelling gap, not a data error.

stewardship_return.summary: In regulated operations, the defensible metric is the one the regulator already compels the customer to file.
stewardship_return.narrative: Northgate did not need to be persuaded that TRIR mattered, nor to build a measurement apparatus for it — the OSHA 300A already existed and was already audited internally. The value engineer's work was attaching a capability to it, not inventing a metric. This is the strongest available position for LVRF: a customer's regulatory filing is a source the customer cannot dispute and a vendor cannot fabricate. Candidate for the regulated-industry pack, and for CVAF where the same substitution applies to compliance-driven commercial cases.
